environment: synthetic-staging partial proof plus repository review

email_verification.evidence: Synthetic student and operator confirmed through captured Mailtrap SMTP messages with no pre-confirmation session.
email_verification.observed_result: Both identities confirmed successfully through allowed callbacks.

login.evidence: Confirmed synthetic student signed in with password.
login.observed_result: Password login returned a session only after confirmation.

account_recovery.evidence: Recovery was delivered through Mailtrap and preserved the provider subject.
account_recovery.observed_result: Old password failed and the replacement succeeded without changing subject.

server_identity_validation.evidence: Online provider validation returned the same subject as login.
server_identity_validation.observed_result: getUser validated the access token and stable provider subject.

operator_mfa.evidence: Synthetic operator enrolled and verified TOTP.
operator_mfa.observed_result: Challenge verification promoted the session to aal2.

mfa_server_enforcement.evidence: Current requireAdmin trusts the role claim in the locally issued access token and does not require a current allowlist record or aal2.

current_session_revocation.evidence: Synthetic operator global signout revoked session continuation.
current_session_revocation.observed_result: Global signout completed and online validation no longer accepted the captured session.

stale_access_token.evidence: Online provider validation rejected the captured access token after global signout; offline JWT acceptance remains an application risk.
stale_access_token.observed_result: getUser rejected the captured token after revocation.

eligibility_independent_of_provider.evidence: Repository inspection shows ride and booking services call application-owned eligibility services, but the available focused ride test mocks those checks. No public HTTP plus PostgreSQL demonstration has yet proved rejection and approval independently of provider role or editable metadata.

operator_allowlist_independent_of_provid.evidence: The current API has no operator allowlist model; requireAdmin authorizes from a role embedded in the application JWT.

abuse_controls.evidence: Provider endpoint limits and CAPTCHA support are documented, and the API has a shared auth rate limiter, but configured staging behavior and reset/login thresholds were not measured.

secure_cookies.evidence: The current API sets HttpOnly, production Secure, SameSite=Lax cookies. Supabase SSR behavior has not been exercised behind the intended staging proxy.

origin_csrf.evidence: SameSite=Lax is present, but no explicit Origin validation or synchronizer/double-submit CSRF defense protects cookie-authenticated mutations.

auth_outage.evidence: No controlled provider outage was injected. The required policy is safe reads where identity is locally verifiable and denial of protected mutations when current session or MFA assurance cannot be established.

provider_subject_mapping.evidence: The decision record specifies a unique (provider, provider_subject) mapping to the existing stable users.id; application foreign keys remain unchanged.
provider_subject_mapping.procedure: Review the Stable identity mapping section against pilot-spec.md user story 68 and the current users.id foreign-key model.
provider_subject_mapping.observed_result: The proposed mapping keeps provider subjects separate and leaves every application relationship attached to users.id.

duplicate_missing_email.evidence: The decision record requires a normalized-email collision inventory before migration, rejects provider identities without a usable verified email from automatic claiming, and never treats an obfuscated duplicate-signup response as ownership proof.
duplicate_missing_email.procedure: Compare the Stable identity mapping procedure with Supabase Identity Linking documentation for duplicate and unverified identities.
duplicate_missing_email.observed_result: The procedure stops on normalized-email collisions and routes missing or unverified email identities to manual review.

account_claim_fallback.evidence: The decision record selects controlled claim/reset as the default because password transfer has not been rehearsed; only pre-inventoried stable users may be attached.
account_claim_fallback.procedure: Review the Controlled claim/reset fallback procedure against pilot-spec.md user story 68 and the unknown deployed password baseline.
account_claim_fallback.observed_result: The fallback preserves users.id, requires verified email ownership, audits the link, invalidates legacy sessions, and stops ambiguous claims for review.

limits_smtp_costs.evidence: Primary documentation was checked on 2026-09-23: Free includes 50,000 MAU and basic MFA but pauses inactive projects; built-in SMTP is best-effort, restricted, and currently two messages/hour. Pro starts at USD 25/month; SMTP provider cost remains an operator decision.
limits_smtp_costs.procedure: Read the dated Supabase pricing, custom SMTP, rate-limit, session, and backup sources recorded below and compare them with the 20–30-person pilot and recovery objectives.
limits_smtp_costs.observed_result: Free is sufficient only for development proof; custom SMTP and an approved recovery arrangement remain required costs/decisions for pilot operation.

export_restore.evidence: CLI logical export and auth-schema migration are documented. Free has no managed backups; no export plus clean-project restore rehearsal was run, so RPO/RTO suitability is unproven.

sources.title: Backup and Restore using the CLI

recommendation.rationale: Reject Supabase Auth for pilot adoption now. It remains a viable candidate only after the live staging, application authorization, stale-token, CSRF, outage, and restore requirements in the decision record pass.
remaining_requirements: Extend the synthetic staging proof to the remaining application authorization, browser security, outage, abuse-control, and recovery checks.
Implement stable subject mapping, a current operator allowlist, server-enforced aal2, current-session checks for protected mutations, and explicit CSRF/origin enforcement.
Rehearse logical export and restore, then choose a paid or separately operated backup workflow that can meet the pilot recovery objectives.
Approve an SMTP provider and recurring cost before production use.
